nodes.title: Linux
nodes.description: Command-line navigation, files, permissions, processes and basic administration.

nodes.title: Networking
nodes.description: The TCP/IP model and the role of IP addresses, ports and protocols; DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, TCP vs. UDP, routing, NAT and basic packet flow.

nodes.title: Programming
nodes.description: Python for automation, parsing, HTTP interaction, small security tools and challenge solving.

nodes.title: Foundation checkpoint
nodes.description: Before moving deeply into exploitation you should be comfortable using a terminal, navigating a Linux filesystem, changing permissions, inspecting processes, using basic network commands, reading HTTP traffic, and writing small Python scripts.

nodes.title: TryHackMe
nodes.description: Guided, beginner-friendly learning paths and practical rooms. Good for building a structured foundation.

nodes.title: OverTheWire Wargames
nodes.description: Game-style exercises that build command-line, Linux and security problem-solving skills.

nodes.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
nodes.description: Free interactive web-security labs covering major web vulnerabilities and techniques.

nodes.title: pwn.college
nodes.description: Hands-on security education with a strong focus on low-level systems and exploitation concepts.

nodes.title: CyLab Academy
nodes.description: Formerly known as picoCTF.

nodes.title: CTFlearn
nodes.description: Capture-the-flag challenges across categories; useful for practicing problem solving.

nodes.title: CryptoHack
nodes.description: Interactive cryptography challenges, useful once basic programming and mathematical foundations are in place.

nodes.title: Linux / Enumeration
nodes.description: Files, permissions, processes, services, basic network enumeration.

nodes.title: Web
nodes.description: HTTP, sessions, authentication, access control, input handling, common web vulnerabilities.

nodes.title: Crypto
nodes.description: Encoding vs encryption, modular arithmetic, hashes, classical and modern primitives.

nodes.title: Reverse Engineering
nodes.description: Program behavior, assembly basics, debugging, static/dynamic analysis.

nodes.title: Binary / Pwn
nodes.description: Memory layout, stack/heap concepts, debugging and exploitation in controlled labs.

nodes.title: Forensics
nodes.description: Files, metadata, logs, packet captures and artifact analysis.

nodes.title: CTF-focused channels
nodes.description: CTF-focused explanations, walkthrough-style learning and exposure to challenge-solving approaches.

nodes.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
nodes.description: Use the labs systematically. Suggested sequence: HTTP basics → authentication/access control → injection → client-side issues → advanced topics.

nodes.title: Core concepts to understand
nodes.description: Requests, responses, headers, cookies, sessions, authentication vs. authorization, access control, input validation, injection, and client-side vs. server-side behavior.

nodes.title: Foundations of Cryptography — NPTEL / IIIT Bangalore
nodes.description: Course by Prof. Ashish Choudhury.

nodes.title: Network Security — NPTEL
nodes.description: Course by Prof. Gaurav S. Kasbekar. Useful for connecting cryptographic ideas with network-security applications.

nodes.title: CryptoHack
nodes.description: Pair coursework with interactive challenges to reinforce concepts.

nodes.title: NetworkChuck
nodes.description: Use as an accessible source for networking, infrastructure and current technology topics.

nodes.title: NFSU CyberSecurity Study Material
nodes.description: A supplementary self-study repository. Treat it as a reference library rather than a linear curriculum.

nodes.title: How to keep learning
nodes.description: Follow one structured curriculum at a time; learn the concept, reproduce it in a lab, solve a challenge, write a short summary, and build small projects.

nodes.title: Weeks 1–2
nodes.description: CLI, filesystem, permissions, processes, text processing, basic shell scripting.

nodes.title: Weeks 3–4
nodes.description: TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, ports, routing, packet flow; basic troubleshooting.

nodes.title: Weeks 5–6
nodes.description: Syntax, files, modules, requests, sockets, parsing and automation.

nodes.title: Weeks 7–8
nodes.description: PortSwigger Academy labs; HTTP, authentication, access control and injection concepts.

nodes.title: Weeks 9–10
nodes.description: OverTheWire + TryHackMe; solve beginner challenges without walkthroughs first.

nodes.title: Weeks 11–12
nodes.description: Choose one: pwn.college, cryptography/CryptoHack, web security or CTF specialization.

nodes.title: I can use Linux comfortably from the terminal.

nodes.description: Burp / PortSwigger style request inspection.

nodes.title: I have solved beginner CTF challenges across more than one category.
nodes.description: Multiple CTF categories attempted.

nodes.title: I understand the difference between encoding, hashing and encryption.
nodes.description: Crypto foundations.

nodes.title: I have completed hands-on labs without relying on step-by-step walkthroughs.
nodes.description: Independent lab work.

nodes.title: I have chosen a specialization to explore next.
nodes.description: Pick a track: pwn, crypto, web or forensics.
